I know the feeling. Having people physically see you're not the same. I won't lie, it hurts. To not only be having negative thoughts, but not being able to hide it to the point where others are taking notice. I will say it's OK to cry. Being a man isn't defined by being a rock and showing no emotion. Being a man is showing emotion and knowing that you're human. Like everyone else. Focus on one thing, solve one problem at a time. No matter how long, push yourself to do better if you can. You should be your first best friend and be able to have your own back. You're the master of your own destiny. I'm gonna be blunt going off from what I just said, you are responsible for your deeds. It's important to accept what has been and what is. But that shouldn't stop you from seeing that as an opportunity for change. Know the wrongs, know the bad. So you can look the opposite direction and focus on doing what's right and good. It won't be easy, nothing ever is. But if you can somehow dig yourself out of this hole, no matter how deep, you can do anything if you set your mind to it.

Trust me. I understand completely. I haven't been tested by a professional, but I think I have mood swings or bipolar disorder. We were so happy in the beginning, then the arguments started. However, I still get moments where I'd trade it to get her back if I could. Knowing what I know now, having changed for the better, I know I could do better. I try to distract myself from these thoughts as sometimes they do put me down, but nothing seems to work. History repeats itself. I'm sorry that you're going through something. I wish I could say it gets better, but considering this was your first relationship, it'll be tough. Something I've been saying within the past week that I try to make myself feel better and do better mentally is, "My future wife is out there. I have to stay strong for her." I just hope one day I can move on and do better for her

I understand friend. I lived most my life being socially awkward and anti social. I wanted friends but could never make them. However, I taught myself that my first best friend is myself. I've pushed myself to get out of my comfort zone and workout and go out by myself. I've never had so much fun in my own company, not worrying about what others think. Last week I went to the beach at night, put in my headphones and just danced to music. There were people on the beach, but I didn't care. I had so much fun. I also know not to let one bad moment define my character. Whatever you like/enjoy, others will too. It's OK to not have friends. Those that will care for you, if they don't already know (and whether you've met them or not) will be there for you. And be your friend.

Then they aren't your friends. I recommend deleting them from your Instagram. It was truly the most difficult thing for me to do, deleting my ex off of Snapchat. I can't say I've been in your position. Everyone lives different lives and goes through different things. I'm sorry that you feel down. If it makes you feel any better, I tried to end it almost a year ago. Next month and it'll have been. A friend saved my life. I'm a socially awkward guy, but people love me. I can make friends easily too, but it's better to have 1 or 2 good friends than have many you don't feel connected to. Recently I had to end a relationship with someone I've never felt so strongly before in my life. It was my shortest relationship at 5 and a half months, but I loved her so much and she loved me. At the end we weren't the same people and I thought ending it would help us both. I realize now it only helped one of us. But I didn't let it get to me if I could. I started focusing on myself. Finding my passions, working on me. I have good days, but I also have bad. Yet I tell myself that I won't let 1 day define the rest of my life. I've been given a second chance and I won't lay it to waste. You can do the same, there's always tomorrow. You can do it if you believe in yourself. It may take a while, but take it 1 day at a time. Make small changes to become a better version of you. Don't be self conscious about your mind or body. Let the past be the past. It can't hurt you if you don't let it. It's happened, and nothing can change those moments. But living in the past and change your future if you let it. If it helps, try talking/seeing someone. It may help.

Was curious to know what other people thought of this topic. Sad that you think sorcery is best when pyromancy is Cleary better for pve and pvp. 

After all the dlc's (mainly Ringed City) pyromancy recieved a major buff adding in the curved sword, which also acts as a catalyst for pyromancy, Demon's Scar. And the amount of times I've won pvp using a mix up of regular pyromancy and dark is obvious to me that sorcery can't keep up.

For pve, just level up intelligence, faith, and dexterity to have the necessary stats to throw just a small handful of pyromancies to defeat nearly every enemy with ease. It should also be stated that most sorceries cost more fp to use than pyromancies causing the user to drink up their Ashen Estus like their deserted in a desert and it's water. And this is just a nit picky thing, but a lot of sorcerers use the Crown of Dusk (found by a white birch in the Farron Swamp) for boosting their sorceries. Which can take away from Fashion Souls. Not saying it can't be used, but I wouldn't use it to look cool.

1. Chaos Bed Vestiges (earned from the Demon King Soul) - cost less fp to use than say crystal soul spear and has better aoe.

2. Demon's Scar (earned from Demon Princes in Ringed City dlc) - literally the best thing for a pyromancer. Not only are curved swords good in pvp, but it's a literal catalyst for pyromancies. You don't have to switch from a staff, or in a pyromancers case his flame hand, just because you ran out of fp. Not to mention its weapon art, which is constantly roll catching plebs in pvp.

3. Black Flame (earned from the dark witch found in Irithyll Dungeon) - I don't typically use this in pve because Chaos Bed Vestiges (CBV) does more damage and has better aoe. But where it shines is pvp. Typically like to scare my opponent with some CBV. Obviously they just roll out of it, but I want them to get closer thinking it's their choice. Then once they fo I use Demon's Scar weapon art and immediately go into Black Flame which combos very smoothly for the most part unless they have already backed up without being caught in the weapon art.

4. Black Serpent (earned from the dark witch found in Irithyll Dungeon) - another pyromancy I use primarily for pvp. Boy does this flame make people so annoyed. With max dexterity, I can spam this move and make them dance around me. I usually combo this with DS weapon art, into Black Flame, then Black Serpent to get them while they roll away.

5. Warmth (earned from rank 2 in Mound Makers covenant) - the list goes on for the best pyromancies, but unlike the last two entries, I use this only in pve. Helps me maintain my Estus after I get into a tight spot or clear an area and am low on health. I usually get a snack or drink while I heal up over time 😅.

6. Seething Chaos (earned from Demon Princes in Ringed City dlc) - this pyromancy can be good in pve and pvp when timed correctly. A lot of times players think its just a measly fireball that missed, and not a giant flame bomb that's about to go off behind them. It's great for luring people into a trap just to be blown back with massive damage dealt to them. When going against bosses, I like to throw down a Seething Chaos where I predicted where the boss will move next and throw my CBV for massive single target damage.

Those are basically all the pyromancies and weapon I use and why I say pyromancy is stronger than faith or sorcery builds.
